Add a small amount of salt, then gradually add water while mixing to evenly hydrate the flour. Continue adding water until small clumps begin to form when the flour is squeezed by hand. (For 500g of rice flour, use about 150ml of water.) Steam the prepared rice flour mixture for about 30 minutes. To check if it is fully cooked, insert a chopstick into the center. If no dry flour sticks to the chopstick, it is ready. Once steamed, knead the dough thoroughly until it becomes smooth and elastic. Roll and shape the dough into long garaetteok (Korean rice cake sticks). *Note:* Since this homemade version is made without the specialized machines used in rice cake shops, the texture may not be as chewy as commercially made garaetteok. Kohakutou - Japanese Crystal Candy 🍬  If you’ve seen people buying the Silky Gem brand of these candies…I need you to know how cheap it is to just make them yourself at home. Recipe below! Ingredients: ½ cup water  1 tsp agar agar powder (3g) 1 cup sugar (215g) Flavor (e.g. lychee in this video)  Food coloring 1. Dissolve agar agar powder in water and bring to a simmer and stirring til dissolved.  2. Add in sugar, stir until dissolved and then mix in your desired flavouring. Simmer (small bubbles) for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a syrupy texture. Be careful not to over boil (it will spill over and make a mess). 3. Pour into a square or rectangular heat resistant container (or into candy molds) and let cool for 5-10 minutes. *Tip: if there is microfoam on top, simply use a spoon to skim it off 4. Add food coloring into whatever design or color scheme you like. 5. Cool in fridge for 2-3 hours until completely set, then remove from the container and use a knife to cut into whatever shapes you like. Tip: pile up any cuttings to form unique clusters. 6. Place on parchment paper and let dry on the counter for 4-7 days. As it dries the moisture leaves the surface and causes the sugars to crystallize, forming a crispy exterior while keeping a jelly like consistency inside! Store in airtight jars.
